{{Short description|Mathematical category}}
In mathematics, a '''fusion category''' is a [[category (mathematics)|category]] that is [[abelian category|abelian]], [[linear category|<math>k</math>-linear]], [[semisimple category|semisimple]], [[monoidal category|monoidal]], and [[rigid category|rigid]], and has only finitely many isomorphism classes of [[Glossary of category theory#simple object|simple objects]], such that the monoidal unit is simple. If the [[ground field]] <math>k</math> is [[Algebraically closed field|algebraically closed]], then the latter is equivalent to <math>\mathrm{Hom}(1,1)\cong k</math> by [[Schur's lemma]].

==Examples==
The [[Representation theory of finite groups|Representation Category of a finite group]] <math>G</math> of cardinality <math>n</math> over a field <math>\mathbb K</math> is a fusion category if and only if <math>n</math> and the characteristic of <math>\mathbb K</math> are coprime. This is because of the condition of semisimplicity which needs to be checked by the [[Maschke's theorem]].

==Reconstruction==

* Under [[Tannaka–Krein duality]], every fusion category arises as the representations of a [[weak Hopf algebra]].
* Every fusion category admits a [[Skeletonization of fusion categories|skeletonization]], and so a fusion category can be specified simply by specifying the fusion rules of the underlying fusion ring (note that due to [[Oceanu Rigidity|Ocneanu Rigidity]], this is not a unique specification in general).
